best_moment.what: The closed-case man came back with kueh. Small, human and unexpected, and the one bit I'd tell my friend about.

worst_moment.what: Walking every block for nine days and still losing the ward at 48.2%, with the card saying it was never about me. Felt flat after all that effort.

skip_year.why: Recusing from a tender was just a tick-the-box good-boy choice with not much to chew on. Most of the early years felt the same.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y23 closed-case man came back with kueh
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: He actually showed up again years later with kueh

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y28 asked in Cabinet if ministers should be paid on indicators they set
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: STAND dropped 60 then 46 and I lost the ward the next year

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y2 nominated an officer who later backed me
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The declassified card says that choice raised my ceiling to DPM, and people I trained quote me

answer.held_back_by: Honestly my Cabinet question about pay in Y28. It made peers cool on me and then the ward vote went. Being clean and honest every year also meant nothing risky ever happened, so I plateaued at Minister.
answer.ending_fair_why: I did everything right for 29 years, then one election loss ended it and the card said it was never about me. Not sure what I could have done differently, so it felt a bit random.
answer.chase_next: The DPM ending. The card says my ceiling was DPM, so I'd try the succession route again and maybe be less saintly to see if I get further.
answer.play_again_why: It's a long run for one life and a lot of years were just reading and tapping. I'd come back another day, maybe, but not right now.

tone_breaks.line: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
tone_breaks.note: Felt like the game nudging me about how the civil service is, a bit smug. Also it called my own playthrough boring, which stung a bit.

answer.title_fit_why: The pay package every year was the thing I looked at most, and it's catchier. Confirmed & Substantive sounds like a civil service HR term I don't understand.

DARREN LIM · THE FINAL POSITION
Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough, and it was never going to be about you anyway.

RETIRED AS Minister
AT AGE 54
LIFETIME EARNINGS $26.78M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Senior Minister of State. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 38, in The Officer You Nominated, you chose "Let her decide without hearing from you." It raised your ceiling to Deputy Prime Minister.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
